name_en: Koi no kanroni — carp simmered a long while in sugar, syrup, and soy sauce
summary_ja: ぶつ切りにしたコイを砂糖と水あめ、醤油、酒でじっくり煮こみ、一晩置いて味を含ませる郡山の料理。猪苗代湖の水を引いた溜め池で養殖される臭みの少ない鯉を使い、もとはハレの日の料理だったと伝わる。
summary_en: Carp cut into chunks is simmered a long while in sugar, starch syrup, soy sauce, and sake, then left overnight to soak up the sauce — a dish of Koriyama. It uses carp farmed with little of the fish's usual muddiness in ponds fed by Lake Inawashiro, and is said to have started as festival-day food.
source_title: 鯉の甘露煮 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kyabetsu mochi — stir-fried cabbage tossed with freshly pounded rice cake
summary_ja: 醤油とだし、みりんで炒めたキャベツに、つきたての餅を絡めて食べる郡山市逢瀬地区の料理。米とキャベツを自給していた農家が、どちらも飽きずに食べ切るために考え出したアイデア料理と伝わっている。
summary_en: Cabbage stir-fried with soy sauce, dashi, and mirin is tossed with freshly pounded mochi — a dish from the Ose district of Koriyama. It is said to have been dreamed up by farmers who grew both rice and cabbage for themselves, a way to work through a surplus of each without tiring of it.
source_title: キャベツ餅 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Miso kanpura — small unshippable potatoes fried and glazed in sweet miso
summary_ja: 皮つきのまま茹でた馬鈴薯（かんぷら）を油で炒めてから水を加えて柔らかくし、砂糖と味噌で炒め煮にする古殿町の料理。出荷できないほど小さな芋を家庭で食べ切るための工夫から生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: Small potatoes, boiled skin-on and called kanpura locally, are pan-fried, softened with a splash of water, and finished in a sweet miso glaze — a dish of Furudono. It is said to have grown out of a way to use up potatoes too small to sell, from farms that grew them for shipment.
source_title: みそかんぷら 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Daikon mochi — grated heirloom daikon and rice flour pan-fried like okonomiyaki
summary_ja: 皮に赤い筋が入る会津赤筋大根をすりおろし、刻んだねぎやアミ、米粉と混ぜて焼く郡山の料理。お好み焼きに近い焼き方だが、煮崩れしにくい大根の風味がしっかり残るのが持ち味だという。
summary_en: Aizu akasuji daikon, a heirloom turnip with red-streaked skin, is grated and mixed with scallion, tiny shrimp, and rice flour before being pan-fried — a dish of Koriyama, cooked much like okonomiyaki. Its selling point is the daikon's flavor staying intact, since the variety holds its shape well.
source_title: 大根もち 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Mame kazunoko — flat yellow soybeans tossed with soy-marinated herring roe
summary_ja: 青大豆の一種でひらたく黄みを帯びた「ひやし豆」を一晩水に浸して茹で、酒と醤油に漬けた数の子と和える正月料理。福島県内でつくられるおせちに欠かせない一品として親しまれているという。
summary_en: Hiyashimame, a flat, yellow-tinged green soybean, is soaked overnight, boiled, and tossed with herring roe marinated in sake and soy sauce — a New Year dish. It is said to be a fixture of the osechi spread made across Fukushima.
source_title: 豆数の子 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Anko no tomoae — boiled monkfish tossed with its own pan-fried liver
summary_ja: あんこうの肝をフライパンで炒って味噌と砂糖を加えて練り、ゆでたあんこうの身と切り干し大根に絡める相馬の料理。もとは5月の田植えを手伝ってくれた人たちへのご馳走として振る舞われていたという。
summary_en: Monkfish liver is pan-fried and worked with miso and sugar into a paste, then tossed with boiled monkfish meat and dried daikon strips — a dish of Soma. It is said to have started as a feast served in May to thank neighbors who helped with rice planting.
source_title: あんこうのとも和え 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Ohira — smoke-dried river dace simmered with mountain and river ingredients
summary_ja: 産卵期で腹が赤くなったハヤを焼き干しにしてだしを取り、まいたけや昆布、ごぼう、豆腐と煮込む只見町の正月料理。平たい椀に盛りつけることから「おひら」の名がついたとされ、大晦日に仕込み正月に食べるという。
summary_en: Dace caught with reddened bellies at spawning time are smoke-dried for stock, then simmered with maitake mushroom, kelp, burdock, and tofu — a New Year dish of Tadami. It is said to take its name, ohira, from the flat bowl it is served in, prepared on New Year's Eve to eat the next day.
source_title: おひら 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Shimidofu no tamagotoji — freeze-dried tofu stir-fried with greens and egg
summary_ja: 薄切りの豆腐を寒風に2週間ほどさらして水分を抜いた「凍豆腐」を戻し、地元の葉物野菜「信夫菜」と炒めて卵でとじる福島市南部の料理。北西から吹く強風「吾妻おろし」が凍み豆腐づくりを支えてきたという。
summary_en: Sliced tofu is left out in the cold wind for about two weeks until dried into shimidofu, then rehydrated, stir-fried with the local shinobuna green, and finished with beaten egg — a dish of southern Fukushima City. The strong northwesterly wind called Azuma-oroshi is said to be what makes the drying possible.
source_title: 凍豆腐の卵とじ 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_ja: 打ち豆と切り昆布の煮物
name_en: Uchimame to kirikonbu no nimono — pounded soybeans and shredded kelp simmered together
summary_ja: 青大豆を木づちでつぶして乾燥させた打ち豆と、細かく刻んだ切り昆布を大根や油揚げとともに炒め煮にする会津若松の料理。冬に採れる青物が少ない雪国で、長期保存できる乾物を組み合わせて作られてきたという。
summary_en: Uchimame, green soybeans pounded flat with a wooden mallet and dried, are simmered with shredded kelp, daikon, and fried tofu — a dish of Aizuwakamatsu. In a snow country where winter yields little fresh produce, it is said to have grown out of combining keeping foods with long shelf lives.
source_title: 打ち豆と切り昆布の煮物 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Bodara-ni — bone-dry salt cod, soaked a week and simmered soft over days
summary_ja: かちかちに乾燥させた棒鱈を一週間ほどかけて水で戻し、醤油と砂糖で骨までやわらかくなるまで何日も煮込む会津若松の正月料理。新鮮な魚介が届きにくい内陸で、たんぱく源として重宝されてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Bodara, cod dried bone-hard, is soaked in water for about a week and simmered over several days in soy sauce and sugar until even the bones soften — a New Year dish of Aizuwakamatsu. In an inland city where fresh seafood rarely arrived, it is said to have been valued as a source of protein.
source_title: ぼうたら煮 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Hatto — buckwheat and glutinous rice dough cut into diamonds and boiled
summary_ja: そば粉ともち米粉を等分に合わせて練り、菱形に切って茹で、砂糖と塩で味付けしたじゅうねんをまぶして食べる檜枝岐村の料理。江戸期に粉食が制限された際、こっそり食べていたことが名の由来とも伝わる。
summary_en: Buckwheat flour and glutinous rice flour, mixed equal parts, are kneaded, cut into diamonds, boiled, and coated in sweetened, salted perilla seed — a dish of Hinoemata. One account traces its name to an Edo-period ban on eating milled grain, when it is said to have been made and eaten in secret.
source_title: はっとう 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Ego — seaweed simmered down and set firm, sliced like a savory jelly
summary_ja: エゴ草という海藻を30分ほど煮て溶かし、型に流して冷やし固める西会津の料理。江戸後期に新潟から酒の肴として持ち込まれ、宿場町だった西会津に根づいたとされ、からし醤油をつけて食べることが多いという。
summary_en: Ego-gusa, a seaweed, is simmered for about thirty minutes until it dissolves, then poured into a mold and chilled firm — a dish of Nishiaizu. Said to have been brought from Niigata in the late Edo period as a bar snack and to have taken root in Nishiaizu, once a post-station town, it is usually eaten with hot mustard and soy sauce.
source_title: えご 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Konnyaku no shiraae — simmered konnyaku strips folded into sweetened mashed tofu
summary_ja: 短冊切りにしたこんにゃくとにんじんを醤油と砂糖で煮て水気を切り、砂糖と塩で味つけした豆腐と和える塙町の料理。こんにゃくの産地として知られる塙町で冠婚葬祭の際に作られてきた甘めのおかずという。
summary_en: Konnyaku and carrot, cut into strips, are simmered in soy sauce and sugar, drained, and folded into mashed tofu seasoned with sugar and salt — a dish of Hanawa. Hanawa is known as a konnyaku-growing town, and this sweetish side is said to have been made for weddings and funerals there.
source_title: こんにゃくの白和え 福島県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
